LOOK: UP Diliman University Student Council Chairperson Joaquin Buenaflor, together with Student Regent Dexter Clemente, and Matteo Wovi Villanueva of the Student Christian Movement of the Philippines, held a press conference at Vinzons Hall, Thursday, after Buenaflor was issued a subpoena regarding the Sept. 21 Mendiola protest and threatened with apprehension for noncompliance.

Buenaflor criticized what he described as the government’s attempt to silence dissent, telling President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to study history and recognize that student activists cannot be silenced by a mere issuance of a subpoena.

Addressing the UP community, the USC chairperson encouraged students not to be intimidated by the recent actions against activists.

Clemente emphasized that the filing of subpoenas against student leaders is an infringement of democratic rights. He reiterated that civic organizing and public protest are not crimes but responsibilities that citizens must uphold in times of political and social crisis.

Buenaflor is the fourth student leader to receive a subpoena. 

“Ang lahat po ng ito ay patunay na napakabilis kumilos ng PNP pagdating sa pagigipit sa kabataan, pero pagdating sa mga dambuhalang pagnanakaw sa ating bayan, ang PNP ay tila nagbibingi-bingihan, nagbubulag-bulagan, at patuloy na nananahimik,” said Buenaflor.

The student leaders also announced that UP will hold Black Friday protests tomorrow. 

RELATED: https://t.co/V1pcPzgBeC

Photos by Lemuel Pabalan, Jo Espiritu, and Sarah Gates
